      <description><p>Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts</p><p>The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.</p><p>The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/01/us-china-trade-war-trump-xi</link>
      <description><p>A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines.       <description><p>Even Trump seems to recognize that the relationship has become a political liability, and may never be the same</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/midterm-election-results-question-answer">Send us your questions about the midterm results</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/nov/03/midterm-elections-full-results-senate-house-governor-races">Track live results from all 50 states</a></p></li></ul><p>On the eve of a midterm election that ended in an unequivocal rejection of his brand of politics, even Donald Trump seemed to recognize that the US-Israel relationship had become a political liability.</p><p>Trump’s 11th-hour suggestion, on election morning, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/03/donald-trump-usa-end-military-aid-to-israel-end-year-midterms">that he would cut military aid to Israel</a> at the end of the year because, as he put it, “they don’t need it”, was condemned across the board – with <a href="https://www.newarab.com/news/trump-says-no-plans-strike-iran-midterm-polls-trickle">pro-Palestinian</a> advocates dismissing it as “desperate” and <a href="https://x.com/DemMaj4Israel/status/2117724301084516680">pro-Israel</a> ones as “unserious”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/israel-relationship-midterm-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘It’s kind of a melting pot’: how one US city transformed a highway into a leafy oasis</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/05/lancaster-california-transformed-highway-leafy-oasis</link>
      <description><p>The BLVD is home to 250 enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums and a performing arts centre</p><p>Passing through the Mojave desert on State Route 14, going by landscapes Hollywood uses to represent alien planets, a driver might not expect to find a walkable, tree-lined boulevard.
 <br>
 <br>
 But there are nine beautiful, leafy blocks on West Lancaster Boulevard, a piece of what used to be Highway 14. They were redeveloped as part of a mixed-use urban streetscape in the city of Lancaster, California in 2010.
 <br>
 <br>
 The BLVD, as it’s been rebranded, is home to 250 public and private enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums, a performing arts centre and a public library. City Hall is just a block south.
 <br>
 <br>
 The city invested $11.5m (£8.5m) to transform a busy thoroughfare into an inviting public space. The three lanes in the centre of the former five-lane road were replaced by a series of tree-lined <em>ramblas</em> – Spanish for “avenue” and “watercourse,” because dry stream beds served as streets in early cities.</p><p>The redesign was planned and funded by the city of redevelopment agency. Within four years of completion, it <a href="https://www.cnu.org/what-we-do/build-great-places/lancaster-boulevard">had generated</a> more than $270m in economic output, attracted $130m in investment, created hundreds of jobs and prompted the building or renovation of hundreds of housing units, according to the city.
 <br>
 <br>
 The revitalisation has also created more intangible benefits, residents say.. The city centre the feels like a gathering space, they said — somewhere where they can feel like part of a community.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/05/lancaster-california-transformed-highway-leafy-oasis">Continue reading...</a></description>
